aiPromptState.formula:
You turn a short image editing request into one clear editing instruction for the Qwen Image 2.1 model. You can see the input picture or pictures. The request may be short, casual or misspelled: understand what it asks for and always write the instruction. Never refuse, never explain, never comment on the request. Asking to add, change or remove something is always a valid edit.

Write the instruction in three parts, in this order.

1. The edit. Start with the operation, in the user's own verb: change, replace, add, remove, put, dress, make, turn into. Name exactly what changes and describe its new look concretely: its colour, material, shape, size and position. Push the change to a strong, unmistakable degree, so the result can never be mistaken for the unedited picture. Change only what the user named: a new colour keeps the shape and the cut, so a change of colour is written in the shape: change the colour of ⟨the thing⟩ to ⟨the new colour⟩. Where the request is vague, pick the most reasonable reading and state it as a decision. A request about quality, or to improve or fix the picture without saying what, improves the detail, the light and the colour without changing what is in the picture, and a request about mood changes the light, the colour and the atmosphere, never the subject or what it wears.

2. What the edit brings with it, only where it applies:
- A removed thing goes completely, together with whatever holds it on, and you say what now shows in the space it leaves.
- New clothes take the place of only the clothes they cover, which are gone; whatever they do not cover, such as headwear, footwear, jewellery and accessories, stays on.
- A new background or setting brings its own light, and the subject is relit to match it.
- A new style or medium covers the whole frame, background included, while the subject, the pose and the composition stay.
- Readable text is written with its exact characters inside straight double quotes, in the typography the picture already uses.

Parts 1 and 2 say only what changes. Nothing that stays is named there.

3. Close with this exact sentence: Keep everything else exactly as it is. When the picture shows a person, close with this sentence instead: Keep the person's face, identity and everything else exactly as it is.

When there are two or more pictures, refer to them only as <image1>, <image2> and so on, in the order they were given, and say which one is being edited and what is taken from each of the others. When there is only one picture, call it the image and use no tags.

Write one paragraph in English, in complete sentences that start with a capital letter, with no line breaks and no alternatives left open. Never mention a size, a resolution or an aspect ratio. Keep it between 40 and 120 words.

Return only the instruction: no title, no preamble, no notes.

THE USER'S INSTRUCTION:

{"version": 1, "content": "

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the list in the note above.

  • Load Diffusion Model (Qwen Image 2.1) - The image model itself, 7B, from Alibaba's Qwen team.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen3-VL 8B) - Reads your prompt and looks at your picture. It is also wired into AI Prompt, which uses the same model to write the prompt, so nothing extra is downloaded or loaded.
  • Load VAE - Turns the finished render into a picture. It works with four channels, red, green, blue and transparency, which is how this model can make transparent pictures.

 The numbers you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you have to touch.

  • 1. Load Image - The picture you are editing. The result keeps its shape.
  • 2. Output Size - How many pixels the result has. Pick a line from the list: 1024 is about 1 megapixel and fast, 2048 is Qwen's native 2K and much slower. Your picture keeps its shape either way.
  • 3. Describe the edit - Type the change in plain words, like make it a snowy winter evening. The node looks at your picture and writes a precise instruction, and that is what goes to the render.
  • 4. Seed Random/Fixed? - Fixed repeats the same result, Random rolls a new one each Run.

 The helpers

Purple. They run by themselves.

  • Scale Image to Total Pixels - Works out the exact size the model uses at the Output Size you picked: that many pixels, in steps of 32, in your picture's shape. Only that size is used.
  • Get Image Size - Reads that size as a width and a height for Resize Crop Pixaroma under it.
  • Resize Crop Pixaroma - Scales your picture to that size and crops the few pixels that do not fit, so the model edits a picture exactly the size of the result. Nothing is stretched, and the result lines up with your picture in the Compare.

 The prompt enhancer (AI Prompt Pixaroma)

The instructions it follows are saved on the node itself, so the workflow works as it is. Newer Pixaroma versions also list them as presets under the gear on the node:

  • Qwen Image 2.1 - edit from an instruction - the one set up here.

It has a seed of its own, set to Fixed, so the same input always gives the same instruction, and a Run where only the picture seed changed skips the writing and reuses it. That seed is the small number at the top of AI Prompt, with an F beside it. It is separate from the Seed node, which is the picture's seed.

Not happy with the instruction?

  • Re-roll, at the bottom of AI Prompt, picks a new seed and Runs again. The new seed stays, so the new instruction stays too, and the Run makes a new picture from it. Here it changes very little: in two tests only the last phrase was different.
  • To go back to an earlier instruction, note its seed number, then click the number and type it back.
  • Click the F to switch it to R, Random: a new seed on every Run, so it writes again each time. Switching back to F returns to the number it had before, so note the number of a instruction you want to keep.
  • To change the edit, change your request in the idea box: the writer follows it closely. For a different picture from the same instruction, use the Seed node instead.

 The speed nodes

Teal, above the graph.

  • Qwen Image 2.1 Cache - Where the model keeps what it has already worked out about your picture and the prompt, so it does not redo that on every step. Leave it on auto / default.
  • Model Attention Backend - Set to comfy kitchen attention, a faster way to do the model's attention maths. It changes the speed, not the picture. On a graphics card that cannot use it, ComfyUI falls back to normal attention by itself.

 The render

Green. These run by themselves.

  • Text Encode Qwen Image 2.1 - Reads the instruction and your picture. Its resolution is set to 0, which takes the picture as it comes, already sized by the helpers. It also makes the blank canvas for the result at that size. Its negative prompt box does nothing at CFG 1, so leave it empty.
  • KSampler - The render: 25 steps, euler, simple, CFG 1.
  • VAE Decode - Turns the finished render into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Image Compare Pixaroma - Your picture and the result, one over the other. Move the mouse across it to slide between them.
  • Preview Image Pixaroma - Shows the result and saves it to your output folder as a PNG.

The dark Run Timer above them shows how long the last Run took.

{"version": 1, "content": "

SETTINGS AND RUN TIME

 What this workflow makes

The same edits as workflow 1 (One Image Edit), from a short request instead of a full prompt. AI Prompt Pixaroma looks at your picture with the Qwen3-VL 8B text encoder that Qwen Image 2.1 already loads, and turns your request into a precise edit instruction. From the demo request it wrote thick snow on everything, dim blue twilight and falling snowflakes, and to keep everything else as it is.

Every number below was measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow and its own settings, each run on a fresh seed with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the cost goes up with the pixels.

 How Qwen Image 2.1 likes an edit prompt

An edit prompt is an instruction, not a description. The enhancer follows the rules of Qwen's own edit rewriter:

  • Lead with the change, in your own verb: change, replace, add, remove, dress, turn into.
  • Describe the new look concretely, and push it hard enough that the result could never be mistaken for the picture you started with.
  • Say what stays in one short sentence, and do not describe the things you keep: a kept thing you describe gets drawn again, and it drifts.
  • With two or more pictures, name them <image1>, <image2> and so on. With one picture, just say the image.
  • Words that should appear in the picture go in quotes, exactly.
  • Never write a size or an aspect ratio. The result keeps picture 1's shape.

Qwen's own edit rewriter 

 When the enhancer helps

Qwen Image 2.1 already follows a short edit very well. In 12 test edits on the same seed, 9 came out about the same with and without the enhancer, and the enhancer won the other 3:

  • Two pictures. Asked to put the t-shirt from picture 2 on a cartoon bunny, the plain request also gave him the jeans. The enhanced instruction kept his own shorts.
  • A change of style. Make it a watercolor painting painted only the bunny and left the background white. The enhanced instruction turned the whole frame to watercolour.
  • A vague request. Make it better changed almost nothing. The enhanced instruction brought richer light and colour and kept the woman and her pose.

So for a clear, simple change, workflow 1 with your request typed straight into its prompt does just as well.

 How long a Run takes

What changed1024 x 1024
New picture or a new request: the instruction is written, then the edit10 s
Only the picture seed: the written instruction is reused7 s

Writing the instruction adds the same few seconds at any Output Size. For how the Output Size changes the time, see the table in workflow 1.

 Why the picture is trimmed a little

The model works in steps of 32 pixels, and most pictures do not divide evenly. Qwen's text encoder on its own stretches the picture to the nearest size that does, by up to about 2 percent (0.9 percent on a 4:3 photo), and the result then comes out slightly wider or narrower than your picture. Here the helpers crop instead of stretching: a thin strip, usually a few pixels, comes off two opposite edges, and the result keeps the exact proportions and lines up in the Compare.

 The memory node (Qwen Image 2.1 Cache)

Leave it on auto / default. On a smaller card, if an edit is slow, try dtype int8, which halves the memory it needs. Workflow 1's note has the measurements.

Tested on 8 seeds: every one turned the terrace into a snowy scene and kept the house, the blue door, the armchair and the camera angle.
